examples.question_text:
A population of beetles increases at a rate proportional to the number $N$ present. Water in a vessel decreases at a rate proportional to the volume $V$ remaining. A hot object cools in a room at $24^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ at a rate proportional to its temperature difference from the room.
Write a differential equation for each situation, using positive proportionality constants and defining the time units.
examples.solution_text:
For the beetles, let $t$ be time in days and $k_1>0$.
$\dfrac{dN}{dt}=k_1N$.
For the water, let $t$ be time in minutes and $k_2>0$.
$\dfrac{dV}{dt}=-k_2V$.
For the object, let $T$ be its temperature in degrees Celsius, $t$ time in minutes and $k_3>0$.
$\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-k_3(T-24)$.
When $T>24$, the temperature difference is positive and the rate is negative.

examples.question_text:
A block of ice has mass $m$ kg after $t$ hours and satisfies $\dfrac{dm}{dt}=-0.3m^{2/3}$, with $m(0)=27$.
Find $m(t)$, the time when half its initial mass remains, and the interval for which the melting model applies. Give the half-mass time to two decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
For $m>0$, separate the variables and integrate.
$\begin{align*}m^{-2/3}\,dm&=-0.3\,dt\\ \int m^{-2/3}\,dm&=\int-0.3\,dt\\ 3m^{1/3}&=-0.3t+C\end{align*}$
Using $m(0)=27$ gives $C=9$.
$\begin{align*}3m^{1/3}&=9-0.3t\\ m^{1/3}&=3-0.1t\\ m&=(3-0.1t)^3\end{align*}$
Half the initial mass is $13.5$ kg.
$\begin{align*}\sqrt[3]{13.5}&=3-0.1t\\ t&=10\left(3-\sqrt[3]{13.5}\right)\\ t&\approx6.19\ \mathrm{hours}\end{align*}$
The ice disappears when $3-0.1t=0$, giving $t=30$ hours. The melting formula applies for $0\le t\le30$; afterwards the mass stays zero.

examples.question_text:
A cylindrical tank drains according to $\dfrac{dh}{dt}=k\sqrt h$, where $h$ is the water depth in centimetres and $t$ is time in minutes. Initially $h=144$; after $4$ minutes, $h=64$.
Find the physically valid value of $k$, the depth formula and the time when the tank empties.
examples.solution_text:
The depth decreases, so $k<0$. For $h>0$, separate and integrate.
$\begin{align*}h^{-1/2}\,dh&=k\,dt\\ 2\sqrt h&=kt+C\end{align*}$
Using $h(0)=144$ gives $C=24$. Apply the later depth before squaring.
$\begin{align*}2\sqrt{64}&=4k+24\\ 16&=4k+24\\ k&=-2\end{align*}$
Thus $2\sqrt h=24-2t$, so $h=(12-t)^2$ for $0\le t\le12$. The tank empties after $12$ minutes.
Squaring first would also produce $k=-10$, but $24+4(-10)<0$ cannot equal $2\sqrt{64}$. That value would empty the tank before the stated observation.

examples.question_text:
A metal block warms in a room at $32^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. Its temperature $H$ satisfies $\dfrac{dH}{dt}=k(H-32)$, where $t$ is in minutes. Initially $H=8$; after $6$ minutes, $H=20$.
Find $k$ and $H(t)$. Find when the temperature reaches $29^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.
examples.solution_text:
The constant solution $H=32$ does not satisfy the initial condition. For the required solution, separate and integrate.
$\begin{align*}\dfrac{dH}{H-32}&=k\,dt\\ \ln|H-32|&=kt+C\\ H&=32+Ae^{kt}\end{align*}$
Using $H(0)=8$ gives $A=-24$.
$\begin{align*}20&=32-24e^{6k}\\ e^{6k}&=\dfrac12\\ k&=-\dfrac{\ln2}{6}\end{align*}$
Therefore $H(t)=32-24e^{-(\ln2)t/6}$, for $t\ge0$.
For $H=29$:
$\begin{align*}29&=32-24e^{-(\ln2)t/6}\\ e^{-(\ln2)t/6}&=\dfrac18\\ t&=18\ \mathrm{minutes}\end{align*}$
The negative value of $k$ makes the block approach room temperature.

examples.question_text:
Atmospheric pressure $P$ kPa satisfies $\dfrac{dP}{dh}=kP$, where $h$ is altitude in metres. The pressure is $60$ kPa at $2000$ m and $30$ kPa at $6000$ m.
Find $k$ and the pressure at ground level, to the nearest kPa.
examples.solution_text:
The constant solution $P=0$ does not satisfy the data. Separate and integrate.
$\begin{align*}\dfrac{dP}{P}&=k\,dh\\ \ln|P|&=kh+C\\ P&=P_0e^{kh}\end{align*}$
The observations give $60=P_0e^{2000k}$ and $30=P_0e^{6000k}$. Divide to eliminate $P_0$.
$\begin{align*}\dfrac{30}{60}&=e^{4000k}\\ k&=-\dfrac{\ln2}{4000}\end{align*}$
The units of $k$ are per metre.
$\begin{align*}P_0&=60e^{-2000k}\\ P_0&=60\sqrt2\\ P_0&\approx85\ \mathrm{kPa}\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
An inverted conical tank has height $18$ cm and top radius $6$ cm. It is initially full. Water evaporates at a rate proportional to the area of its circular surface. After $4$ hours, the depth is $15$ cm.
Let $r$ be the water-surface radius and $h$ the depth, both in centimetres. Given $V=\dfrac13\pi r^2h$, form and solve a differential equation for $r$. Find the emptying time and state one limitation of the model.

A population $W$, measured in hundreds of animals, satisfies $\dfrac{dW}{dt}=0.04W-3$, where $t$ is in years.
Interpret both terms and find the equilibrium population in animals.
examples.solution_text:
The term $0.04W$ represents natural growth at $4\%$ of the current population per year. The term $-3$ represents removal of $300$ animals per year.
At equilibrium the rate is zero.
$\begin{align*}0.04W-3&=0\\ W&=75\end{align*}$
Since $W$ is measured in hundreds, the equilibrium population is $7500$ animals.

examples.question_text:
The mass $Q$ grams of a product after $t$ minutes is modelled by $Q=\dfrac{240t}{t+6}$, for $t\ge0$.
Show that $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=\dfrac{(240-Q)^2}{1440}$, check the initial mass, and state the limiting mass.
examples.solution_text:
Differentiate the proposed function.
$\begin{align*}\dfrac{dQ}{dt}&=\dfrac{240(t+6)-240t}{(t+6)^2}\\ &=\dfrac{1440}{(t+6)^2}\end{align*}$
Now substitute the function into the right-hand side.
$\begin{align*}240-Q&=240-\dfrac{240t}{t+6}\\ &=\dfrac{1440}{t+6}\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}\dfrac{(240-Q)^2}{1440}&=\dfrac{1440^2}{1440(t+6)^2}\\ &=\dfrac{1440}{(t+6)^2}\end{align*}$
Both sides agree, so the function satisfies the differential equation.
$Q(0)=0$ grams. Also $Q=\dfrac{240}{1+6/t}$ for $t>0$, so $Q\to240$ grams as $t\to\infty$.

examples.derivation: Proportional growth gives N'=k1N; proportional loss gives V'=-k2V; cooling towards 24°C gives T'=-k3(T-24), with all three constants positive.
Integration gives 3m^(1/3)=9-0.3t, hence m=(3-0.1t)^3. Half-mass time is 10(3-cuberoot(13.5))≈6.19 hours. Nonnegative cube root requires 0≤t≤30; zero mass thereafter also satisfies the DE.

Integration gives 2sqrt(h)=kt+24. The later observation gives 16=4k+24, so k=-2 and h=(12-t)^2 for 0≤t≤12. The squared-equation alternative k=-10 violates the original nonnegative square-root relation.
Separation gives H=32+Ae^(kt). Initial data give A=-24; later data give e^(6k)=1/2 and k=-ln(2)/6 per minute. H=29 requires e^(kt)=1/8, giving t=18 minutes.
Separation gives P=P0e^(kh). Dividing observations gives e^(4000k)=1/2, so k=-ln(2)/4000 per metre. P0=60sqrt(2)≈84.85 kPa, rounding to 85 kPa.

Similarity gives h=3r and V=πr^3. Combining V'=-kπr^2 with the chain rule gives r'=-k/3 for r>0. Data r(0)=6 and r(4)=5 give k=3/4 and r=6-t/4, reaching zero at 24 hours. The planar cross-section correctly shows matching tank and water proportions; its generic water level is not labelled as the later observation.
The natural growth term is 4% per year; removal is three hundreds of animals per year. Setting 0.04W-3=0 gives W=75 hundreds, or 7500 animals.
The quotient rule gives Q'=1440/(t+6)^2. Since 240-Q=1440/(t+6), the proposed right-hand side equals the same derivative. Q(0)=0 and the limiting mass is 240 grams.
